description: High oxygen sensitivity requires low OTR packaging
reason: High oxygen sensitivity indicates significant risk of oxidative degradation (lipid oxidation, colour change, vitamin loss). Packaging must restrict oxygen ingress — low OTR is required.
notes: Qualitative rule. Numeric OTR threshold depends on product-specific oxygen sensitivity data not available in this prototype. Operator: HIGH oxygen sensitivity → LOW OTR requirement.

description: Medium oxygen sensitivity requires medium OTR packaging
reason: Medium oxygen sensitivity indicates moderate oxidation risk. A medium oxygen barrier is appropriate — overly restrictive barrier may not be cost-justified.

description: High moisture sensitivity requires low WVTR packaging
reason: High moisture sensitivity indicates product quality loss from moisture uptake or loss (e.g. crispness loss in snacks, caking in powders). Low WVTR packaging is required to maintain water activity within acceptable limits.
notes: Qualitative rule. Numeric WVTR threshold depends on product-specific water activity tolerance not available in this prototype.

description: Medium moisture sensitivity requires medium WVTR packaging
reason: Medium moisture sensitivity indicates moderate moisture management needed.

description: High fat content elevates oxidation risk classification
reason: High fat content (especially unsaturated lipids) increases susceptibility to oxidative rancidity. Combined with oxygen exposure, this produces off-flavours and nutritional degradation.
notes: Risk classification rule used by Risk Engine. Not a packaging property requirement directly — feeds into oxidation risk level which then triggers RULE001.

description: CLIMACTERIC respiration class requires gas exchange analysis
reason: Climacteric produce continues to respire post-harvest, consuming O2 and generating CO2 and ethylene. Packaging must permit controlled gas exchange to prevent anaerobic conditions (O2 depletion) and CO2 buildup — both cause quality loss. MAP analysis is required.
notes: Triggers MAP engine for fresh climacteric produce.

description: HIGH respiration class requires gas exchange analysis
reason: High-respiration produce actively consumes O2 and generates CO2. Hermetic or high-barrier packaging would cause rapid O2 depletion and anaerobic fermentation. Controlled atmosphere or breathable packaging required.

description: HIGH respiration class — packaging must NOT be maximum barrier
reason: Respiring produce requires O2 influx to maintain aerobic conditions. Maximum barrier (very low OTR) packaging is CONTRA-INDICATED for fresh produce with high or climacteric respiration class. A controlled intermediate OTR that matches the respiration rate is needed.
notes: This rule OVERRIDES the general HIGH oxygen sensitivity → LOW OTR rule for fresh produce. The MAP engine handles the specific OTR calculation.

description: High microbial sensitivity requires good seal integrity
reason: Products with elevated microbial sensitivity require hermetic seal integrity to prevent post-packaging contamination and maintain modified atmosphere if used.
notes: Applies to fresh produce and microbially-sensitive products.

description: High oxygen sensitivity and high fat both present — elevate oxidation risk to HIGH
reason: Combination of high oxygen sensitivity and high fat content represents maximum oxidative degradation risk. Both conditions must be present for this elevated risk classification.
notes: Risk engine rule. The fat condition is checked separately (RULE005). Combined logic is implemented in the risk engine.

description: NONE respiration — no gas exchange requirement
reason: Processed or non-respiring foods do not require gas exchange packaging. Barrier properties are the primary consideration.
notes: Applies to snacks, processed foods. Used to exclude MAP analysis path.

description: High oxygen sensitivity — good seal integrity required
reason: Effective oxygen barrier requires hermetic seal integrity. A high-barrier film with a poor seal provides no meaningful protection. Seal integrity is a prerequisite for barrier performance.
notes: Sealability requirement linked to oxygen barrier requirement.

description: Medium light sensitivity — light barrier beneficial
reason: Products with light sensitivity benefit from packaging with opaque or light-barrier layers to retard photo-oxidation and pigment degradation.
notes: Metallised or aluminium foil structures provide light barrier. Qualitative requirement.

description: HIGH microbial sensitivity and HIGH moisture — elevated microbial risk
reason: High moisture content combined with high microbial sensitivity creates conditions for rapid microbial spoilage if packaging is breached or does not maintain modified atmosphere.
notes: Risk classification rule. Numeric aw thresholds for microbial growth are food-specific and not replicated as generic values here.
